name: Palal
title: Wall Builder in Jerusalem
summary: Palal, son of Uzai, was one of those who participated in the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls under Nehemiah's leadership. He repaired a section of the wall next to the projecting part of the palace and the watchtower. His contribution is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as part of the collective effort to restore the city after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding of Jerusalem's Wall
keyEvents.description: Palal, son of Uzai, repaired a section of the wall opposite the projecting tower and the upper palace near the guardhouse. His work was an important part of the overall effort to restore Jerusalem's defenses.

keyEvents.title: Nehemiah's Organization of the Work
keyEvents.description: Nehemiah organized the people into groups to rebuild different sections of the wall. Palal was among the many volunteers who took responsibility for their assigned section.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to the Rebuilding
keyEvents.description: The workers, including Palal, faced opposition from enemies such as Sanballat and Tobiah, but continued their work with determination and faith.

keyEvents.title: Armed Work on the Wall
keyEvents.description: Due to threats from enemies, the wall builders, likely including Palal, worked with weapons beside them while building, ready to defend themselves.

keyEvents.title: Completion of the Wall
keyEvents.description: After 52 days, Jerusalem's wall was completed, made possible by the efforts of all the workers, including Palal and his associates.
